threads.thread_goal: Align on promotion scope, target items, and overall objectives.

messages.text:
Kicking off the seasonal promotion corner project for project_pack_ref: Launch of Seasonal In-Store Food Promotion Corner. We have 21 days to get the corner live, so we need to lock the scope and target items quickly.
Two things to align here:
1) Which product categories we want in the corner.
2) What we are aiming for in terms of sales lift and customer experience.
For the assortment and stock plan, we will capture everything in the Seasonal Promotion Assortment and Stock Plan sheet (A1) and track work under T1 and T5.
Initial proposal on categories based on last season and what customers ask for most:
- Ready-to-eat salads and light meals
- Bakery treats (seasonal pastries, small cakes)
- Flavoured drinks and juices that match the season
- A small section of premium snacks for upsell at the till
Please react or comment with what you would add/remove, and any early thoughts on sales and customer experience goals for this corner.

Thanks for starting this. From what I see at the till, customers often grab:
- Small bakery items they can eat on the go
- Chilled drinks
- Something a bit healthier to balance it out
So your list makes sense. I would add:
- A small fruit grab-and-go section (single apples, bananas, small fruit cups)
On goals, could we say:
- Target: at least 15 percent uplift in sales for these items during the promotion
- Customer side: make it easier for people to pick a quick snack plus drink in under 2 minutes
We can refine the numbers once we start filling A1 under T1, but this gives us a starting point.

From the food side, I would just flag that ready-to-eat salads and open bakery items will need tighter control on dates and handling.
For categories, I support:
- Salads and light meals
- Bakery
- Chilled drinks
- Fruit grab-and-go
I would be careful with anything that needs heating or complex handling at the corner itself, given the constraint on not disrupting store opening hours.
On objectives, maybe we can split:
- Sales: uplift target like 15 percent as suggested
- Waste: keep write-offs on these items within our usual range, not higher
- Customer experience: clear pricing and allergy info so we do not get confusion at the counter.
We can reflect these in A1 when we define minimum and target stock levels in T1 and when we confirm deliveries in T5.

Agree with the list so far. From my kitchen days, seasonal soups can sell well, but they are harder to keep at the right temperature on the shop floor, so maybe we keep those in the usual area and just signpost them from the corner.
For the corner itself, I would focus on items that are safe at ambient or standard chilled conditions.
On goals, could we also track:
- Attach rate: how often a customer buying from the corner also adds a drink or snack from the same area
That might help us later when we work on upsell scripts.

I like the idea of a small premium snacks section. People often ask for something a bit nicer when they are buying for others.
Maybe we define categories like this in A1 for T1:
1) Everyday grab-and-go (fruit, basic snacks)
2) Treats (bakery, premium snacks)
3) Light meals (salads, sandwiches)
4) Drinks (juices, flavoured water)
On objectives, I would keep it simple for the team:
- Sell more of these items
- Keep the corner full and clean
- Make it easy for customers to understand what is on offer
We can translate that into more precise numbers in the sheet.

So far I see strong support for these categories:
- Fruit grab-and-go
- Bakery treats
- Light meals (salads, sandwiches)
- Chilled drinks
- Premium snacks
Before we lock this, any objections to excluding hot items from the corner itself and just signposting them, as suggested? That will simplify hygiene and avoid extra equipment.
On objectives, I like the idea of:
- Sales uplift target around 15 percent for the items in A1
- Attach rate improvement (more baskets with at least 2 items from the corner)
- Clear pricing and allergy info to avoid confusion
If no one disagrees, I will capture this in A1 as part of T1 and T5 and we can treat that as our working objective set.

No objection from me on excluding hot items from the corner. It will be easier to keep the area tidy and avoid queues.
On the objectives, I would just add that we should track customer comments about clarity of pricing and product info, so we can see if we are meeting the experience goal.
Happy for you to write this into A1 under T1.

I am also fine with not having hot items in the corner. That will reduce the risk of temperature issues and complex cleaning.
For the categories, the five you listed cover what we can handle well with our current supplier contracts and storage.
On objectives, I support the sales uplift and attach rate focus, plus a hygiene and waste angle: we should aim not to increase waste compared to our usual levels for these items.
Once we start T5 and confirm deliveries, we can check if any supplier constraints force us to adjust the list.

All good from my side. The five categories feel manageable.
On the goals, maybe we can keep a simple note in the corner for us: full, fresh, fast. Full shelves, fresh products, fast service. Then the detailed numbers live in A1 and the tracker later.

Agree with the five categories and with leaving hot items out of the corner.
On objectives, I think we should also keep in mind the daily routine: if the goals are too complex, it will be hard to explain in the briefing. So I like the idea of a clear sales uplift target plus a simple message about customer experience.
No further changes from me.

Thanks all. Summarising what we have so we can close this:
Product categories for the promotion corner:
1) Fruit grab-and-go
2) Bakery treats
3) Light meals (salads, sandwiches)
4) Chilled drinks
5) Premium snacks
We will not place hot items directly in the corner; we will only signpost them.
Objectives for the promotion period:
- Sales: aim for around 15 percent uplift on the items listed in A1, plus better attach rate (more baskets with at least two items from the corner).
- Customer experience: quick and easy choice, clear pricing and allergy info, no confusion about what is on promotion.
- Operations: keep waste and hygiene within our usual standards.
I will record this in A1 as part of T1 and T5 and treat it as our agreed scope and objectives.
Summary looks good to me. Once you have updated A1, share the link here so we can start filling in specific items and quantities under T1.
Aligned with the summary. When we move into T5 and speak with suppliers, I will double-check that we can get enough stock for each of the five categories within the 21-day window and flag any gaps.
No further comments from me. Happy to move on to the detailed list in A1 and start thinking about how we group these on the shelves for T2 later.
All good. Once the categories are in A1, I can help check past sales for similar items so we set realistic minimum and target stock levels for T1.
I will update A1 with the agreed categories and draft initial stock ranges for each by tomorrow, then we can iterate together under T1 and start supplier checks under T5.
Perfect, once that is in place I will start filling in expected daily sales per item so we can see if the 15 percent uplift target is realistic.
And I will prepare a simple list of supplier contacts per category so that when we start T5 we can move quickly on confirming availability and delivery dates.

threads.thread_goal: Define the visual layout and operational constraints for the corner.

messages.text:
I have put together a first draft of the promotion corner layout for the Promotion Corner Visual Merchandising Layout guideline (A2), based on the categories we agreed in A1.
High-level idea:
- Top shelf: premium snacks and small bakery treats at eye level
- Middle shelves: light meals and fruit grab-and-go
- Bottom shelf: heavier drinks crates and multipacks
- Side panel: clear signage with prices and a simple seasonal message
This is captured as a sketch under T2. Before we finalise, I need your feedback on:
1) Does this work with the actual fixtures and floor space we have?
2) Where exactly in the store should we place the corner so we do not block aisles or cause congestion?
Please share any concerns or suggestions so we can refine and then move towards approval for T6 setup.

Thanks for drafting this. From a flow point of view, I would suggest we avoid putting drinks only on the bottom shelf. Some customers will not want to bend down.
Maybe we can:
- Put single chilled drinks at hand level
- Keep heavier multipacks lower
On location, my first thought is the area near the entrance on the right, but that can get crowded at peak times. Another option is the space opposite the bakery, which has good visibility but less through-traffic.
We should also check with the store manager that the chosen spot does not break any safety rules about exits or sightlines.

On the fixtures, the current gondola we use near the bakery has four shelves and a small header. It should fit the categories if we:
- Use the header for the seasonal message
- Keep the top shelf for lighter items only (no heavy drinks)
For the floor space, we need to leave enough room for trolleys to pass. The spot opposite the bakery that 311830 mentioned usually has better flow and less risk of blocking the entrance.
From a hygiene angle, I would keep fruit and open bakery items away from the very bottom shelf to reduce dust and accidental kicks.

I like the idea of using the space opposite the bakery. People already slow down there to look at bread, so the corner would be a natural extension.
On the layout, could we group items by occasion:
- Quick breakfast (pastries, coffee-flavoured drinks)
- Light lunch (salads, sandwiches, water)
- Treats (premium snacks, sweet drinks)
That might make it easier for customers to build a small meal without thinking too much.

One concern: if we put the corner opposite the bakery, we need to check the distance to the nearest power point for any chilled units. The current chiller for drinks is closer to the entrance.
Maybe we can:
- Keep the main chiller where it is
- Use the bakery-opposite space for ambient and short-life items that do not need power
We should confirm with the store manager which fixtures we can move before we lock the layout in A2 and start T6.

Good points. How about this adjusted layout for A2 under T2:
- Header: seasonal message and simple price cues
- Top shelf: premium snacks and some bakery treats
- Second shelf: light meals
- Third shelf: fruit grab-and-go and single chilled drinks (lighter bottles and cans)
- Bottom shelf: heavier drink multipacks only
On location, I like the idea of using the space opposite the bakery for the main corner and keeping the existing chiller near the entrance for drinks, with clear signage linking the two.
We will still need the store manager to sign off on the exact footprint and any fixture moves.

The adjusted layout works better for access and hygiene.
On the footprint, we should define it clearly before we ask for sign-off. Suggestion:
- Use one full gondola opposite the bakery for the main corner
- Use the existing chiller near the entrance as a linked drinks zone, with matching signage
We can mark this in A2 and then book 15 minutes with the store manager to confirm that we are not blocking any key paths or exits.

Agree with the shelf order and the split between the bakery-opposite gondola and the entrance chiller.
We should also think about cleaning access for T6 and later: leaving a small gap between the gondola and the wall will make it easier to sweep and wipe down.
Once the store manager confirms the spot, we can add a small note in A2 about cleaning access so it is not forgotten.

From a customer journey point of view, the occasion-based grouping can still work within your shelf plan:
- Top shelf: treats
- Second shelf: light meals
- Third shelf: fruit and drinks that go with both
We can reflect that in the small shelf labels when we get to signage.
No issues from me on the proposed location and footprint.

I am fine with the layout and the split between the gondola and the chiller.
For the exact footprint decision, I suggest we prepare a quick sketch with measurements in A2 and then ask the store manager to confirm. That way T6 setup will be straightforward on the day.

Let me summarise the proposal so we can close on layout and location:
Layout (for A2, T2):
- Header: seasonal message and key price points
- Top shelf: premium snacks and selected bakery treats
- Second shelf: light meals (salads, sandwiches)
- Third shelf: fruit grab-and-go and single chilled drinks
- Bottom shelf: heavier drink multipacks only
Location and footprint:
- One full gondola opposite the bakery as the main promotion corner
- Existing chiller near the entrance used as a linked drinks zone, with matching signage
- Ensure enough space for trolleys and cleaning access.
If everyone agrees, I will update A2 accordingly and then book time with the store manager to confirm the footprint so we can treat this as the final layout for T6.
Summary matches what we discussed. Once the store manager confirms the footprint, I am comfortable treating this as the approved layout for the promotion corner.

Agreed. Please add a small note in A2 about keeping fruit and open bakery off the bottom shelf and leaving space for cleaning, then I am happy to call this final from a hygiene and practicality point of view.
Looks good to me. Once the store manager signs off on the gondola position, we can move ahead with T6 planning.

No objections. The split between the main corner and the chiller should help with traffic flow.
Happy to proceed with this as our layout and location, pending store manager confirmation.

Great, I will update A2 with the final layout details and the gondola plus chiller footprint, then share it with the store manager for sign-off. Once they confirm, we will treat D3 and D4 as closed and move on to detailed T6 setup planning.

threads.thread_goal: Lock customer interaction scripts and hygiene routines.

messages.text:
I have drafted two documents for review:
- Customer Interaction and Upsell Script (A3) under T3
- Food Safety and Hygiene Routines for the Promotion Corner (A5) under T7, plus a first version of the Daily Stock, Hygiene, and Display Checklist (A4) under T4.
Key points in the customer script:
1) Greeting and quick question about what the customer is looking for
2) Simple guidance by occasion (quick breakfast, light lunch, treat)
3) One upsell suggestion (for example, adding a drink or fruit)
4) Clear mention of any key allergens when relevant.
Key points in the hygiene routines:
- Cleaning frequency for shelves and surrounding floor
- Handling rules for open bakery and samples
- Date checks and removal of expired or damaged items.
Please read through and comment here on anything that is unclear or missing before we lock these for the team briefing.

I went through A3. The flow is clear and not too long, which is good.
Two suggestions:
- In the greeting, maybe add an option for when the customer is in a hurry, something like: 'If you are in a rush, I can point you to the quickest options.'
- For upsell, we could give two examples per category so staff do not repeat the same line all day.
On A5, the routines look solid. I just want to confirm: for open bakery, are we using tongs and paper bags only, or are there any exceptions?

On A5 and A4, from a kitchen perspective I would emphasise:
- Clear handwashing points before handling any open food or samples
- A simple rule for how long samples can stay out before we discard them
- A visible place to record date checks so we do not rely on memory.
The checklist in A4 already covers date checks, but maybe we can add a tick box for samples removed on time.

On A3, I like the structure. Maybe we can add one line to help with price questions, something like: 'Most items here are between X and Y, and the offers are clearly marked on the shelf labels.' That should reduce confusion.
For A4, could we keep the checklist to one page so it is easy to use during busy times? If we add more items, we might need to group them into sections: stock, hygiene, display.

I have a couple of detailed points:
- In A3, for allergy info, we should be clear that staff must check the product label or the info sheet before answering, not guess.
- In A5, for cleaning frequency, we might want to tie it to specific times (for example, before opening, mid-shift, and before closing) so it is easier to follow.
Also, for T4, we should assign who is responsible for each part of the checklist by shift, otherwise it might get skipped.

Thanks for the feedback.
On A3:
- I will add a short 'rush' version of the greeting.
- I will include two upsell examples per category so the team has variety.
On A5:
- For open bakery, the rule will be tongs and paper bags only, no exceptions. I will make that explicit.
I will also integrate the points from others on handwashing, sample time limits, and clear timing for cleaning into A5 and A4.

Good call on samples. I will add to A5:
- Maximum time samples can stay out
- Clear rule to discard leftovers after that time
And in A4 I will add a simple tick box for 'samples removed on time' so it is easy to track.
For handwashing, I will include a short reminder in the routine and in the checklist header.

On A3, I will add a simple line about price ranges and pointing to shelf labels, as you suggested.
On A4, I will keep it to one page and group items into three sections: stock, hygiene, display. That should make it easier to use during busy periods.

Agreed on allergy info. I will make it clear in A3 that staff must always check the product label or info sheet before answering.
For A5 and A4, I will tie cleaning tasks to specific times: before opening, mid-shift, and before closing.
On T4 responsibilities, I will propose that the opening person handles the first check, mid-shift is done by whoever is on the corner, and closing is done by the late shift, and we can confirm that in the briefing.
Once you have updated A3, could you share a short example of a full interaction from greeting to upsell? That will help us see if it feels natural before we roll it out in T3.

Here is a quick example based on the updated A3:
- Greeting: 'Hi, are you looking for a quick snack, a light meal, or just a drink today? If you are in a rush, I can point you to the quickest options.'
- Guidance: If they say light meal, we point to salads and sandwiches and mention one or two bestsellers.
- Upsell: 'A lot of people pair this with a fruit cup or a flavoured water from the shelf just here.'
- Allergy: 'If you have any allergies, I can check the label or our info sheet for you.'
Does this feel natural enough for the team?

The example reads well and is easy to remember. I think A3 is in good shape now.
On A5 and A4, once you add the timing and sample rules, I would be comfortable treating those as our standard routines for the corner, as long as the food safety officer does not raise any issues when they review them.

I like the tone of the script. It is friendly but not pushy.
On the hygiene side, as long as the sample time limit and handwashing reminders are clearly written in A5 and visible in A4, I am happy to follow these routines.

Script example works for me. It should be easy to adapt to different customers.
For A4, grouping the checklist into stock, hygiene, and display will help us run through it quickly at each time slot.

I have now updated A3, A5, and A4 with all the points discussed and sent them to the food safety officer for a quick review.
Unless they request changes, can we agree to use this customer script and these hygiene routines for the promotion corner and brief everyone on them in T9?

From my side, yes. Assuming the food safety officer is fine with A5 and A4, I am happy to confirm that we will use the current version of A3 as the standard script for all sales assistants at the corner.
Agreed. Once we get the green light from the food safety officer, we can print A3 and A4 and keep them at the corner, and use A5 as the reference in the briefing.

threads.thread_goal: Plan the launch date, team briefing, and daily routines.

messages.text:
We need to lock the go-live date, plan the team briefing, and assign owners for the daily checklist and sales tracking.
Proposal:
- Go-live date: two weeks from today, which keeps us within the 21-day deadline and gives time for T1, T2, T5, and T6.
- Team briefing (T9): the day before go-live, 30 minutes before opening, to walk through A2, A3, A4, and A5.
- Daily checklist (A4, T4): three checks per day (opening, mid-shift, closing).
- Sales and feedback tracker (A6, T8): updated once per day after closing.
Who can cover setup on go-live day (T6) and who is willing to own the daily checklist and A6 updates on a rotating basis?

Two weeks from today works for me for go-live, and the pre-opening briefing the day before is fine.
I can:
- Help with T6 setup on go-live morning
- Take the opening checklist slot (A4, T4) on most weekdays
For A6, I can do the first week of daily updates after closing so we get into the habit.

The proposed go-live date is fine for me as long as suppliers confirm deliveries in time under T5.
I can:
- Join T6 setup on go-live day, focusing on checking dates and placement against A1 and A2
- Take the mid-shift checklist slot (A4, T4) on my shifts
For A6, I can support with entering any customer comments I hear during the day.

Go-live in two weeks works for me.
I can:
- Help with T6 setup, especially cleaning and arranging the shelves according to A2
- Take the closing checklist slot (A4, T4) on the days I close
For A6, I am happy to rotate weekly with others after the first week.

I am also fine with the proposed go-live date and the briefing the day before.
I can:
- Cover T6 setup if anyone is off that day, or support with signage and labels
- Take mid-shift or closing checklist slots when 128528 or 433060 are not on
For A6, I can take over the daily updates in the second week of the promotion.

Good, sounds like the date works for everyone.
Before we confirm, we should double-check two things:
1) That T1 and T5 will be complete in time so we have stock and confirmed deliveries.
2) That the store manager is available for a quick walk-through of the corner after T6 setup on go-live day.
If those are fine, I suggest we lock the go-live date and the briefing time.

On T5, I have already contacted the main suppliers and they confirmed they can deliver the key items a few days before the proposed go-live. I will document the exact dates and quantities in A1 and flag any risk.
So from the supply side, I am comfortable with the proposed date.

On T1, we have the item list and minimum and target stock levels drafted in A1. I will finalise any missing quantities by tomorrow so we are ready for go-live.
I can also check with the store manager today about their availability for a quick walk-through after T6 setup.

Once the store manager confirms, we should add the briefing time and go-live date into the rota notes so everyone sees it.
For T9, I suggest we cover: overview of A1 and A2, walk through A3, and then run through A4 and A5 so everyone knows the routines.
Agree. Once we have confirmation from the store manager, we can send a short message to the wider team with the go-live date, briefing time, and who is doing which checklist slot and A6 updates.

Store manager has confirmed they are fine with the proposed go-live date and can join us for a quick walk-through after T6 setup. They are also ok with a 30-minute briefing the day before, before opening.
So from their side, we are good to lock the date and time.

Great, then let us confirm:
- Go-live date: two weeks from today, with T6 setup in the morning before opening and a quick walk-through with the store manager.
- Team briefing (T9): the day before go-live, 30 minutes before opening, covering A1, A2, A3, A4, and A5.
I will treat this as our official launch plan.

On daily routines and ownership, based on what you all offered, here is a proposal:
- Opening checklist (A4, T4): 186687 on weekdays, 439564 on weekends.
- Mid-shift checklist (A4, T4): 128528 on their shifts, 439564 as backup.
- Closing checklist (A4, T4): 433060 on their closing shifts, 439564 as backup.
- Sales and feedback tracker (A6, T8): 186687 does daily updates in week 1, 439564 in week 2, then we rotate if the promotion continues.
If everyone is ok with this, we can treat these as the assigned owners.
I am fine with being owner for opening checks on weekdays and A6 updates in week 1.
Happy to take the mid-shift checklist on my shifts and support with any notes for A6 during the day.
I am ok with owning the closing checklist on my closing days.
Fine with the weekend opening, backup mid-shift and closing, and taking A6 updates in week 2.

Thanks all. With the go-live date, briefing time, and daily owners confirmed, we have what we need to proceed.
I will document this in A4 and A6 so it is clear who does what each day.

threads.thread_goal: Review early performance and agree on adjustments.

messages.text:
We have completed the first week of the promotion, so I have updated the Promotion Sales and Customer Feedback Tracker (A6) under T10.
Highlights:
- Strong performers: bakery treats and premium snacks are above the expected daily sales from A1.
- Steady: chilled drinks are close to target.
- Underperforming: fruit grab-and-go and some of the lighter salads are below the minimum levels we planned.
Customer feedback from A6:
- People like the look of the corner and find it easy to spot.
- A few comments that some fruit packs look too similar in price to the bigger packs elsewhere.
- Some customers asked for more savoury snack options.
We need to decide:
1) Which underperforming items we replace or discount further.
2) Whether we adjust the layout in A2 or the script in A3 based on this feedback.
Please share your thoughts so we can agree on changes and update T10.

Looking at A6, the fruit cups and one of the salad lines are clearly below what we planned in A1.
My suggestion:
- For fruit: keep the best-selling format and either discount or remove the slowest one, replacing it with a savoury snack option that customers asked for.
- For salads: reduce the facing for the slowest salad and give more space to the top seller.
On layout (A2), we might move the stronger items slightly higher on the shelf to make them more visible.
On the script (A3), we could add one more savoury snack upsell example.

From what I have seen on the floor, customers often pick bakery and snacks quickly, but they hesitate more with fruit cups and some salads.
I agree with:
- Dropping the slowest fruit cup format and replacing it with a savoury snack, maybe nuts or savoury crackers, as long as it fits our contracts in A1.
- Reducing the slow salad line and giving more space to the bestseller.
On pricing confusion, maybe we can adjust the shelf labels so the price difference between small fruit packs and larger packs elsewhere is clearer.
For A3, I can add a savoury snack upsell line to the script.

I support replacing the weakest fruit item with a savoury snack. From a food side, savoury nuts or baked crackers are easy to handle and have decent shelf life.
On layout, we could:
- Put the stronger items closer to the middle of the shelf
- Group savoury snacks together so they are easy to spot
For the script, adding a savoury upsell line will help us respond to the feedback about wanting more savoury options.

Looking at A6, I also noticed that some customers commented that they did not realise certain items were part of the promotion.
Maybe we can:
- Add a small coloured tag on the shelf labels for all promotion items
- Update the script in A3 to include a short line like: 'Everything on this shelf is part of our seasonal corner.'
On underperformers, I agree with focusing on the best fruit and salad lines and bringing in one savoury snack to test.

So far we seem aligned on:
- Removing the slowest fruit cup format
- Reducing the slowest salad line
- Adding one savoury snack line
- Tweaking layout and script.
Before we decide exactly which items to change, can we confirm which fruit cup and salad are the slowest in A6 and whether we have a suitable savoury snack in A1 that we can bring in quickly?

Based on A6:
- The mixed berry fruit cup is the slowest fruit item.
- The quinoa salad is the slowest salad.
In A1, we already have a savoury nut mix listed as a backup item under the premium snacks category, so we can bring that into the corner without new contracts.
I suggest:
- Remove the mixed berry fruit cup from the corner and replace it with the savoury nut mix.
- Reduce the quinoa salad facing to one and give the extra space to the top-selling salad.
I can update A1 and A2 accordingly and adjust the script in A3 with a savoury upsell example.

That sounds like a good, low-risk adjustment.
On pricing clarity, I would also:
- Add a small note on the fruit shelf label to highlight the value compared to larger packs
- Make sure the promotion tags are consistent across all items in the corner.
If we agree on these changes, we should record them in T10 as our first mid-course adjustment.

I am fine with removing the mixed berry fruit cup and reducing the quinoa salad. The savoury nut mix should work well and is easy to manage.
For layout, I can help move the products around so the new snack sits near the premium snacks and is easy to see.

Agreed with the specific item changes.
On the script, adding a savoury upsell line like 'Many people add a savoury nut mix with this drink or salad' should help.
I can also help update the shelf labels and add the coloured promotion tags.

Let me summarise the proposed adjustments so we can close on them:
Items:
- Remove mixed berry fruit cup from the corner.
- Reduce quinoa salad facing to one.
- Add savoury nut mix as a new savoury snack option.
Layout and signage (A2):
- Give more space to the top-selling salad.
- Place savoury nut mix near premium snacks.
- Add coloured promotion tags to all promotion items.
- Clarify fruit pricing on shelf labels.
Script (A3):
- Add a savoury snack upsell example.
If everyone agrees, we will implement these changes and record them in T10 as our first mid-course adjustment.

Summary matches what we discussed. I support making these changes.
We should monitor the nut mix and the adjusted salads in A6 over the next week to see if performance improves.

Agreed. I will:
- Update A1 with the item changes
- Adjust A2 for the new layout
- Update A3 with the savoury upsell line
and note these changes in T10 as our first adjustment set.
I will handle the physical move on the shelves and make sure the new layout matches A2 once it is updated.
I will update the shelf labels and add the coloured promotion tags, and I will keep an eye on customer comments about the new savoury option for A6.

Thanks all. With this, we have agreed which underperforming items to replace or reduce and how to adjust the layout and script based on week-one feedback.
I will log these decisions and the follow-up actions in T10 and keep tracking results in A6.
